findings.summary: 3D bioprinting uses layer-by-layer deposition of bioinks—cells mixed with hydrogels and nutrients—to fabricate tissue-like structures. The process spans pre-bioprinting (imaging, cell isolation, scaffold design), bioprinting (extrusion or projection of bioinks guided by medical scans), and post-bioprinting (incubation and bioreactor stimulation to mature tissue and promote vascularization). Multiple printing technologies exist, including extrusion, stereolithography, and magnetic bioprinting, each suited to specific cell types and tissue targets.

mechanisms.title: Layer-by-layer bioink deposition
mechanisms.explanation: Cells are mixed with liquefied hydrogel bioinks and deposited in successive layers using printer cartridges. The bioinks provide oxygen and nutrients while the layer-by-layer approach builds tissue-like structures guided by tomographic reconstructions of patient scans.

mechanisms.title: Post-bioprinting maturation via bioreactors
mechanisms.explanation: After printing, mechanical and chemical stimulations in bioreactors send signals to cells to control tissue remodeling and growth. Different bioreactor types—convective flow, compression, microgravity—are ideal for specific tissues such as cartilage.

unknowns: Precise micro-scale organization of functional and supporting cell types within printed constructs
Long-term viability and function of bioprinted constructs after transplantation
Full replication of native extracellular matrix composition and solubility factors
Integration of printed tissues with host vasculature and nervous systems in vivo
